key_insight: PureVision improves medical VLM interpretation by adding geometry-aware visual supervision so lesion phenotypes and their anatomical relationships are preserved in the embedding space.
clinical_relevance: This could make AI-assisted image reading more reliable for multi-phenotype lesions, supporting better grounding in reports and question answering.
method: PureEyes learns visual representations with ideal spatial distributions that encode anatomy hierarchies and phenotype-subclass relationships.
PureNeurons maps images into the learned latent space and selectively aggregates lesion-specific anatomical and phenotypic evidence.
The framework is designed to address sparsity in lesion-related representations during medical VLM interpretation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements on LIDC-IDRI, CBIS-DDSM, and 3DReasonKnee for lesion grounding and phenotype characterization in visual question answering and radiology report generation.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of geometric supervision and the learned latent-space design, so generalization across scanners, organs, and annotation styles may need careful validation.
paper_title: Geometry-Supervised Visual Representation Learning for Multi-Phenotype Lesion Interpretation in Medical VLMs
